messages:
deploy-bot: Starting staged rollout v3.7.0 -> 10% traffic across eu-west, ap-south. Change window: 02:00-04:00 UTC. Rolling percent: 10% stable for 20m check. Release notes: <internal/release/3.7.0>

sara: Holding — seeing auth 502s tick up in the sample stream. Not huge but trend is concerning: 0.2% -> 1.1% in last 6m. Anyone seeing backend errors? :rotating_light:

paul: I see increased 95p latency on the auth proxy in ap-south around the same time. Correlates with batched token refreshes. Pulling logs now.

olivia: Confirming release included a change to the auth batcher window (batch_size cap lowered). Could be interaction with proxy keepalives. Release note snippet: "auth: reduce batch timeout to 40ms"

paul: Logs show a spike of upstream 502s at 2026-03-23T02:12:04Z from auth-legacy-1. Stack traces point to connection resets when batching > 8 requests.

mike: Paging oncall to weigh in. If this is an infra/backpressure issue we should stop and pin. @oncall-bot status?

oncall-bot: @sara, @paul, @olivia — oncall is nora. Pager escalated. Nora has been notified.

nora: Oncall here. Quick check: are these client-side or server-side 502s? If server-side likely regression in batcher change. If client-side, could be routing.

paul: Full trace shows server-side 502s from auth service (auth-legacy). No obvious network flaps. Repro locally by simulating batched refresh load. Repro steps in gist: 
```
# repro: simulate 200 users with batch window 40ms
python tools/load_auth.py --users 200 --batch-window 40
```

olivia: Given repro and timing, this is likely the new batch timeout. We pushed that change in this release.

sara: Proposal: Pause the rollout (stop further ramp to 25%), pin traffic back to v3.6.9 for eu-west & ap-south, and create a rollback patch for auth batcher ASAP. Thoughts?

mike: Agreed. We should also throttle incoming requests to auth temporarily (increase retry/backoff) and set a canary flag for the batcher change so it can be toggled without full rollback.

nora: Action plan I can execute now: 1) pause rollout; 2) pin region routes to 3.6.9; 3) revert batcher change in a hotfix branch; 4) run targeted load test. I need an explicit go/no-go.

paul: Commands to run: 
```
# pause further percent increases
deployctl rollout pause --version=3.7.0 --strategy=percent
# pin eu-west & ap-south to previous stable
deployctl pin --version=3.6.9 --routes=eu-west,ap-south --reason="auth 502 spike"
```

sara: I approve. Execute now. :thumbsup:

nora: Running pause + pin. exec id: exec-20260323-001. Will post status when done.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused by nora (exec-20260323-001). No further traffic increases will be applied.

deploy-bot: Pins applied: eu-west -> v3.6.9, ap-south -> v3.6.9.

nora: Pins confirmed. Creating incident ticket INC-20260323-45 and assigning to olivia & paul for hotfix.

olivia: Starting revert PR for batcher change, testing on staging. I'll tag @sara when ready for verification.

paul: Running extended load tests against staging hotfix branch. Will report success/failure in this thread.

sara: Summary/decision: STOP rollout. Pause further percent ramps. Pin regions eu-west/ap-south to v3.6.9. Hotfix + staging validation before any resume. Follow-up: add a retrospective blameless note about batch window tests.

mike: Noted. I'll update release notes and notify product that we aborted the percent ramp.

nora: Closing the stop/go call — monitoring for any residual errors. If spike clears and tests pass we can reconvene for a limited re-release with canary flag.

deploy-bot: Thread closed for now. If you need immediate action use `deployctl` or reopen thread.
